# Carlos Volweides — Fullstack Engineer

Carlos Volweides is a fullstack engineer based in Caracas, Venezuela.
Specializes in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python (FastAPI), React, Next.js, Astro, React Native.
Focuses on clean architecture, Domain-Driven Design (DDD), event-driven systems, and LLM integration.
Available for remote work as of August 2026.

## Experience

- Digitan Agency (July 2025 – August 2026): Fullstack Developer, remote for Córdoba, Argentina.
  Built end-to-end web and mobile applications for logistics platforms, billing systems, and
  multi-app integrations using Next.js, React Native, FastAPI and PostgreSQL.

## Projects

- **Frida** (shipped): Clinical and administrative management for geriatric care homes — patient
  records, vital signs, medication dosing, staff shifts and billing. Built solo end to end at
  Digitan Agency. 12 bounded contexts on a three-layer DDD architecture with an event bus over
  pyventus; 356 pytest tests and 38 Playwright E2E tests.
  Stack: Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, pyventus, Playwright.

- **Atlas Protocol** (MVP, closed beta): AI-powered platform for generating personalized technical
  courses. Study path generation, per-module content, and a chat agent grounded by system prompts
  with responses streamed over WebSocket.
  Stack: Next.js, Supabase, Vercel AI SDK, FastAPI.

- **Repositorio UGMA** (deployed, internal): Institutional thesis repository for Universidad Gran
  Mariscal de Ayacucho. Search for students, approval workflow for coordinators.
  Stack: PHP, JavaScript, SQL, NoSQL.

- **Luxdata** (shipped): Hotel management system with reservations, check-in/out, billing, room
  blocking, and occupancy dashboards. Stack: React, Node.js, Express, Tailwind CSS, MySQL.

## Education

## Site

This portfolio is built with Astro, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, deployed on Vercel.
Source code: available on request.

Trilingual: Spanish is served at the root (/, /projects, /projects/<slug>), English under
the /en prefix (/en, /en/projects, /en/projects/<slug>) and Brazilian Portuguese under the
/pt prefix (/pt, /pt/projects, /pt/projects/<slug>). All three languages carry the same
content and are linked via hreflang.
